h: Shabbos Holds the Holiness of All the Festivals

p: In this parashah it is written,
before the section of the festivals,
and on the seventh day a Shabbos, etc."
"What does Shabbos have to do with the festivals?
To teach you that whoever desecrates, etc.,
and whoever keeps the festivals, etc.,
is as though he kept the Shabbosos."
if he did not keep the Shabbosos,
keeping the festivals will not help
that although ceasing on Shabbos carries stoning
And Shabbos is "first of the callings of holiness,"
"These are the appointed times of Hashem, callings of holiness,"
and afterward the festivals are listed.
And the holiness of Shabbos is fixed
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
from the creation of the world,
אַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה אָז שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת
even though there were then no Shabbos-keepers.
On the contrary, the Bnei Noach were commanded,
and a Ben Noach who keeps Shabbos is liable to death
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן מַתָּנָה זוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and afterward He gave this gift to Yisrael
But the holiness of the festivals
Pesach at the Exodus from Egypt,
through their having sinned with the Calf
and being forgiven on Yom Kippur;
and afterward Sukkos, the time of joy,
"And you shall take, etc., and you shall rejoice, etc."
And it is stated (in Vayikra Rabbah 30:2):
"Whoever takes the palm branches in his hand,
we know that he is the victor."
And so too the sukkah is named for
כִּי בַסּוּכּוֹת הוֹשַׁבְתִּי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"For in sukkos I settled Bnei Yisrael, etc." (Vayikra 23:43);
"Whoever is of the root and stock of Yisrael
And of Rosh Hashanah too it is said
כִּי חוֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט וְגוֹ׳
"For it is a statute for Yisrael, a judgment, etc.":
although all who come into the world
pass before Him like a flock of sheep
"a judgment of the God of Yaakov";
"For I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,"
it is then in their power
to instill holiness into the festivals.
is included in "a calling of holiness":
instill holiness into the day of Shabbos,
With food and with drink, etc."
that one must instill holiness into Shabbos.
That is: in the Second Tablets,
"And you shall remember that you were a slave
in the land of Egypt, etc.;
therefore Hashem your God commanded you
to make the day of Shabbos":
one must instill holiness into Shabbos
from the side of Yisrael as well,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח)
in the manner of what is said (Koheles 1:18),
"For in much wisdom is much anger."
all the holiness of the festivals,
and sanctified it above all times."
for every day has in it
give Him the blessing appropriate to it."
has a blessing particular to that day;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
And so the holy Zohar states
and each one has in it
And Shabbos corresponds to the seventh attribute;
and it is stated (in Sefer HaBahir):
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
in which the holiness of all of them is included:

according to what is written in the holy Zohar
on this parashah (III 94a, end of the side):
and to join with them, etc."
groomsmen of the day of Shabbos;
and this is what we say at the Friday night meal,
And the matter is as we said:
that each day contains a particular holiness
from the holiness of the times.
And I heard from our holy Rebbe,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing,
הֵם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וְיוֹם רְבִיעִי
correspond to the first day and the fourth day;
to the third day and the sixth day.
And he did not explain the reason.
And we are accustomed to say
corresponds to the holiness of Shabbos,
when one counts the days of the festivals,
דְּאָז נֶחְשָׁב חַג הַפֶּסַח לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים
for then Pesach counts as two days,
the first and the last of Pesach;
and then there are six days among the festivals,
and Yom Kippur corresponds to the day of Shabbos.
But when one counts the festivals,
is a festival in its own right;
and then there are six festivals
And he counted Pesach opposite the first day,
שֶׁפֶּסַח נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for Pesach corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to whom the exile of Egypt was told,
"and afterward they will go out with great wealth";
and it corresponds to the attribute of Chesed,
And on the first day the primordial light was created,
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham"
"'Let there be light' — this is Pesach").
Shavuos corresponds to the fourth day,
which is the attribute of Netzach,
שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ
of which Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, is the chariot;
and then is the time of the giving of our Torah,
which he brought down from heaven.
And on the fourth day the luminaries were hung,
and the essential light is the Torah,
corresponding to the five books of the Torah.
Rosh Hashanah corresponds to the second day,
according to what is written in the Tikkunim
and it is the Day of Judgment,
corresponding to the attribute of Gevurah,
corresponding to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him.
And Yom Kippur corresponds to the fifth day,
which is also a day of judgment,
and the court below are aligned";
and it was given to Aharon
for he is the chariot for the attribute of Hod;
for Aharon is the groomsman of the Matronisa,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג נג, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
as is written (in Zohar III 53b, end of the side):
And he is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
"And he shall be a mouth for you,"
"And Torah they shall seek from his mouth."
as they said in the Gemara (Nedarim 22b):
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah, etc.,

and it is stated in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah 46:1):
לֹא הָיוּ אֶלָּא עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת לְבַד
there were only the Ten Commandments,
but in the Second Tablets I give you
And this was given to them then
opposite the fifth day and the attribute of Hod,
of which Aharon the Kohen is the chariot.

of which Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
as is written in the holy Zohar
shall dwell in the sukkos, etc."
the root and holy stock of Yisrael.

that was after Yaakov was born
for then it became clear that
"For in Yitzchak shall seed be called yours"
were called by the name Yisrael,
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
And Shemini Atzeres corresponds to the sixth day
and it is the completion of the first ones;
are bound one to the other."
And this is the attribute of Yaakov and Yosef.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִיא רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
And nevertheless it is a festival in its own right
and it is the absorbing of the holiness of Sukkos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
includes the holiness of all the festivals.
Pesach is the time of our freedom,
and of Shabbos the Gemara states (Shabbos 118b):
and it is derived from what is said (Yeshayahu 30:15),
"In return and rest you shall be saved";
that there be one Shabbos as it should be
And likewise Shavuos is the time of the giving of our Torah,
the Torah was given on Shabbos
are the time of our rejoicing;
and it is stated (in the Sifrei, Beha'alosecha):
"'And on the day of your rejoicing' (Bamidbar 10:10)
"They shall rejoice in Your kingship, etc."
And Rosh Hashanah is called the Day of Remembrance;
and here it is written "And on the day of your rejoicing,"
which is expounded of the Shabbosos,
and the end of the pasuk is
"And they shall be for you a remembrance."
"For it is a statute for Yisrael, etc.,"
that all of a person's sustenance
אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
and each one gives sustenance below,
with which they are blessed on the seventh day, etc."
and of Shabbos it is written (Yeshayahu 56:2),
And on it the Second Tablets were given,
and Shabbos is the attribute of Malchus:
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"the mouth — we call it Torah she'b'al peh";
corresponds to the attribute of Yesod;
and Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant,
as is written in the holy Zohar
which is the attribute of Yesod, Yosef.
And this is "And sanctified it above all times":
includes the holiness of all the times.
that Hashem Yisbarach gave to the day of Shabbos,
which includes the holiness of all the festivals,
from this Yisrael had the power
to instill holiness into times and festivals.
And this is why the pasuk mentioned
before the holiness of the festivals,
and it is "first of the callings of holiness,"
a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,
and from this they instill holiness into the festivals,
as they said in the Midrash
when filled from the holy, becomes holy;
And this was at the Exodus from Egypt,
to sanctify the new months and the festivals.
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar:
for Shabbos is a daughter crowned with the Avos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
the holiness of the three Avos;
and likewise the attribute of Yosef,
(III, in the Tosefta, end of section 8):
the Mussaf of Shabbos corresponds to Yosef;
and both are in Shabbos, as stated.
And this is "to join with them
to guard the holiness of Shabbos
that it not be damaged, chas v'shalom.
they are the holiness of the festivals,
of which the six ushpizin are the chariot;
that each one instill his holiness
for Shabbos is called "a calling of holiness,"
וְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה, בְּמִדְבַּר י, א)
With food and with drink, etc."
in order to complete a hundred blessings,
And it seems that seven kinds of food are needed,
meaning large fish and small ones.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת שָׁם, קיח, ב)
in the manner of what they said (Shabbos 118b):
"With what does one delight in it? etc.,
and one who cannot afford it,
a dish of small fried fish"
And it is as we said,
that the essential delight of Shabbos is with fish,
no prohibition of chelev or gid hanasheh;
and in fowl there is at least
the prohibition of blood and neveilah,
which is not so with fish.
This implies that fish have no
for to every animal, beast and bird
from the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil
but of fish it is not said that she fed them,
since they were then in Gan Eden
And it mentioned large and small fish
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what the holy Arizal wrote
on what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 140b):
and not in my wealth did I eat vegetables"
when he was poor in daas,
and likewise when he became rich in daas,
the holy sparks even from meat.
And so one who is rich
delights in it with large fish,
for he can extract the holy sparks from them;
and when he is poor in daas,
the holy sparks from large fish,
he makes something small in honor of Shabbos,
And this is "and fish with small fry."
